_note: One unit = one lesson path in five steps. Write 'God' (the Muslim view shows 'Allah'). Verses by ref only (shown from src/data/ayahs.json); hadith by id only (shown from src/data/hadith.json). 'about' lines are our own words, never a translation.

intro.muslim: Adam's two sons each brought an offering to God. One gave his best, with care; the other gave the least he could. Only one was accepted. Watch why.
intro.curious: Adam's two sons, known in the Bible as Abel and Cain, each brought an offering to God. One gave his best, with care; the other gave the least he could. Watch which was accepted, and why.

muslim.situation: You volunteer at a food drive. Someone is taking photos for social media, and you notice you work harder whenever the camera points your way.

options.label: Make sure you're in as many photos as possible.
options.feedback: It's natural to want to be seen. But Habil's offering was accepted for something else. Let's see what.

options.label: Notice it, quietly renew your intention for God, and keep working the same either way.
options.feedback: That's sincerity: catching yourself and turning your heart back to God, whoever is watching.

options.label: Stop volunteering: if your intention isn't perfect, why bother?
options.feedback: Scholars warn that quitting good deeds for fear of showing off is a trap too. Fix the intention, keep the deed.

options.label: Ask not to be photographed.
options.feedback: That can help. The deeper fix is in the heart, as the teaching explains.

curious.situation: You volunteer at a food drive. Someone is taking photos for social media, and you notice you work harder whenever the camera points your way.

options.label: Make sure you're in as many photos as possible.
options.feedback: Wanting to be seen is natural. See what Islam teaches makes a good deed count.

options.label: Notice it, and keep working the same whether or not anyone's watching.
options.feedback: That's what Islam calls sincerity: doing good for its own sake, for God, not for the camera.

options.label: Stop volunteering: if your motives aren't pure, what's the point?
options.feedback: Giving up good deeds isn't the answer. Islam says: fix the intention, keep the deed.

options.label: Ask not to be photographed.
options.feedback: That can help, though the real change is inside. The next step explains.

quran.about: God accepts only from those who are mindful of Him.
People were commanded only to worship God, making their devotion sincerely His.
My prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for God, Lord of the worlds.
The righteous feed others for the sake of God alone, wanting neither reward nor thanks.
A warning for those who pray only to be seen.

hadith.about: Every deed counts by the intention behind it.
God looks at hearts and deeds, not appearances or wealth.

insights.text: Habil's offering was accepted because of what was in his heart, not its size (5:27). Sincerity means doing a deed for God alone, not for praise, money or image.
Intention can turn ordinary things into worship: eating to stay strong, sleeping to rise for prayer, working to support a family, when done with God in mind (Bukhari 1).

check.q: How did Habil prepare his offering?
options: He gave the least he could
He brought a healthy ram, gently and with care
He bought it from someone else
check.why: Habil laid down a healthy ram with care; Qabil dropped a bundle of poor grain without a second look.

check.q: From whom does God accept, according to 5:27?
options: From those who are mindful of Him
From those who give the most
check.why: God accepts only from those who are mindful of Him.

check.q: What does the hadith say deeds are judged by?
What does God look at, according to Muslim 2564?
check.why: God does not look at your appearance or wealth, but at your hearts and deeds.

check.q: What do the righteous want when they feed others, in 76:9?
check.why: We feed you only for the sake of God; we want no reward or thanks.

reflection.muslim: Pick one thing you'll do tomorrow anyway: a meal, a chore, a kindness. Before it, say quietly whom it's for.
reflection.curious: Think of something good you did recently. Would you have done it if nobody ever found out?
